label: Articulated Mestiza consciousness and Borderlands epistemology
description: Anzaldúa developed mestiza consciousness to describe a transformative mode of thinking that inhabits the liminal spaces between cultures, breaking down binary dualisms and synthesizing contradictions.
historicalContext: Published in 1987 in Borderlands/La Frontera: The New Mestiza, written in the Texas-Mexico borderlands.
dialecticalTension: Subverts the Western philosophical demand for homogeneous identity by affirming the epistemic fertility of contradiction and multiplicity.

citations.author: Gloria Anzaldúa
citations.quote: The new mestiza copes by developing a tolerance for contradictions, a tolerance for ambiguity... She has a plural personality, she operates in a pluralistic mode.

citations.author: Mariana Ortega
citations.work: In-Between: Latina Feminist Phenomenology, Multiplicity, and the Self

label: Decolonial intersection of the coloniality of power and borderland feminism
description: Anzaldúa's lived border epistemology directly intersects with Quijano's critique of the coloniality of power, inspiring María Lugones's formulation of the 'coloniality of gender'.
historicalContext: The cross-pollination of Chicana feminist thought with Latin American decolonial philosophy in the 1990s and 2000s.
dialecticalTension: Deepens the critique of coloniality by demonstrating how geopolitical and psychological borders fracture gendered, sexualized, and indigenous bodies.

citations.author: María Lugones
citations.work: Heterosexualism and the Colonial / Modern Gender System
citations.quote: In analyzing the coloniality of power, Quijano understands race as a modern classification... I expand this to show how Anzaldúa's borderland critique reveals the coloniality of gender.

label: Synthesized post-structural discursive power with embodied border resistance
description: Anzaldúa engaged with theories of disciplinary power and somatic normalization, transmuting post-structural insights into embodied, decolonial healing practices through the Coatlicue state and Nepantla.
historicalContext: Conceived during Anzaldúa's doctoral studies in literature and feminist philosophy at the University of California, Santa Cruz in the 1980s.
dialecticalTension: Challenges Foucault's secular, Eurocentric pessimism by invoking Indigenous Nahuatl spirituality and creative somatic agency.

citations.author: Gloria Anzaldúa
citations.quote: Coatlicue depicts the contradictory. In her figure is the synthesis of duality... The Coatlicue state is a prelude to a crossing.
